units.text: A HEAD response lacks a response body, per RFC 9112 section 3.2 and multiple RFC citations spanning 1999 to 2022.

citations.title: HTTP/1.1 Explained: RFC 9110 and RFC 9112 Messages, Methods and Security | Safeguard Blog

judgement.reason: The quoted passages support that HEAD responses must not include a message body and cite RFC 2616 (1999) and RFC 9112 (2022). However, none of the passages explicitly attributes this rule to RFC 9112 section 3.2; that section is quoted only about the Host header.

units.text: RFC 9110, 9111, 9112 were published June 2022 and collectively define the HTTP standard, establishing HEAD response rules.

judgement.reason: The passages support that RFC 9110, 9111, and 9112 were published in June 2022 and collectively define HTTP semantics/caching/message syntax, but none of the provided passages mentions HEAD response rules.

units.text: Span 449 from RFC 9112 explicitly states that any response to a HEAD request is always terminated by the first empty line after header fields and cannot contain a message body.

judgement.reason: The passage states exactly that any response to a HEAD request is always terminated by the first empty line after header fields and cannot contain a message body or trailer section.
